card.title: Choose the Precedent
card.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gets the head seat: Grandma or the birthday child? We have traditions for both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Which tradition decides who gets served first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I can divide the pudding once somebody's had the wish.

mechanism: A requires a choice between elder and birthday precedence when attempts to honor both reach an indivisible ceremonial priority.
confusable: Unlike merely solving seating logistics, A must keep asking which tradition governs action.
comparison: A birthday wish creates first-service pressure, unlike handbook/permit scope deciding whether supper can proceed.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
